name: CHAOS-3505 Go parity: StatusMapping loader + both normalizers
$limitation: Every mutation below is CLAUSE-level: it removes or inverts one conjunct, one comparison, one set member, or one ordering decision, never a whole function. Two things are deliberately NOT mutated here. (1) The DECLARED DIVERGENCE on LoadStatusMapping -- Python's source-relative DEFAULT_STATUS_MAPPING_PATH fallback has no Go equivalent, so there is no shared clause to mutate; it is covered by the written note on the function and by callers always supplying a path. (2) The `if typeRaw != ""` / `if statusRaw != ""` truthiness guards: normKey("") is "" and empty keys are never indexed, so removing the guard changes no observable result. Mutating it would report SURVIVED for a reason that is a property of the INDEX, not of the guard, so it is stated here instead of being listed as a fake kill. THIRD DECLARED EXCLUSION (added with the PyYAML-compatibility work): a mutation that changes the CAPITALISATION of a rendered scalar -- "True"->"true", "None"->"none" -- will SURVIVE, and that is a property of normKey rather than a coverage gap: normKey lowercases AFTER pythonStr, so the two spellings collapse to the same index key before anything can observe them. Listing such a mutation would be a FAKE KILL. The repr-branch mutations above are therefore aimed at tag DISPATCH (M21-M27: whether a scalar is a bool/int/float/string at all) and at the NUMERIC FORMATTERS (M28-M32), which are the places where a divergence survives normalization and reaches an index key.

mutations.rationale: _norm_key collapses INTERNAL whitespace runs, not just the ends. This is the exact shape a naive ToLower+TrimSpace port produces, and it silently stops 'In    Progress' from matching the indexed 'in progress'.
The case-folding clause, isolated from M1's whitespace clause. Jira's index holds 'bug'; a raw '  BUG  ' must still find it.

status_mapping.yaml:82 is `- type: bug` (with a space), which YAML parses as a MAPPING. Python indexes it under str(dict) == "{'type': 'bug'}". A mapping node's own .Value is empty, so this mutation drops the entry entirely -- the shape a port gets when it assumes every list item is a scalar. CHAOS-3512 tracks the underlying config defect; this pin is what forces the Python-first fix and the Go re-mirror to land together.

Python's repr prefers SINGLE quotes. Double-quoting yields the key {"type": "bug"}, which differs from Python's {'type': 'bug'} by two bytes and matches nothing. Isolated from M3: the mapping is still walked and a key still produced. Part of the CHAOS-3512 pin set.

Python's dict repr puts a SPACE after the colon. Dropping it is a one-byte divergence that no type checker sees, and it is not covered by M3 or M4 -- the quoting and the walk are both still correct. Part of the CHAOS-3512 pin set.

mutations.rationale: THE ordering clause. Python iterates a dict in insertion (file) order and _index_values is last-wins, so a raw value listed under two categories resolves to the LATER one in the FILE. Sorting simulates exactly what a port that decoded YAML into a Go map suffers: quirks.yaml lists 'Shared Value' under todo then done, so file order resolves it to done while alphabetical order resolves it to todo.

First-wins instead of last-wins. Distinct from M6: the iteration ORDER is still correct here, only the overwrite rule flips. Both the cross-category collision and the provider-overrides-base pass depend on it.
`if not key: continue`. Without it an empty list entry indexes the empty string, which then makes an empty raw status match a category instead of falling through.

Base first, provider second -- that ordering is what makes a provider `statuses` entry an OVERRIDE. Swapping the two passes lets the shared base silently win, so jira's in_progress override of 'Shared Value' reverts to the base category. Re-anchored after the PyYAML rewrite: the mutation now DROPS the base pass entirely, which is the same clause (base categories participate, and do so BEFORE the provider override) expressed against the current control flow. The `_ = baseEntries` keeps the binding used so the mutant BUILDS; without it the compiler rejects the file and the harness reports INVALID, which measures nothing.
`_as_status_category` returning None drops the whole category with no error. Accepting it instead indexes a bogus category name as if it were a real WorkItemStatusCategory.
The `_as_work_item_type` half of M10, on the shared single-section builder that serves status_labels, types and type_labels. A separate clause in a separate function: M10 cannot reach it.

QUIRK 7. Python reads the variable FIRST and lets it replace the caller's argument unconditionally. This mutation implements the SENSIBLE behaviour -- explicit argument wins -- which is precisely the bug-for-bug divergence D16 forbids.

CHAOS-3505, in the FIXING direction. The checked-in config has a linear section that the hardcoded tuple ignores, and this port mirrors that. Building the linear index is the eventual fix, and it must not be able to land silently inside a port whose contract is bug-for-bug parity.

QUIRK 8. typePriority omits the valid types 'pr' and 'merge_request', so a label matching ONLY one of them enters the label arm and then FALLS THROUGH to the type_raw arm. Returning early is what a port assuming the priority list is exhaustive would do, and it changes the answer from the type_raw arm's result to 'unknown'.

The priority ORDER itself, not its membership. Swapping the top two entries is invisible unless a case supplies both labels at once -- and it is the very inversion the Linear provider's hand-rolled _type_from_labels fallback already has in production (see the PR body's divergence table).
'Prefer more terminal states' is the documented rule for the status label arm. Reversing it makes an item labelled both todo and done report todo, understating completion in every rollup.

The default arm is `provider_key in {"github", "gitlab"}`. Dropping the gitlab disjunct sends every unmatched GitLab work item to 'unknown' instead of 'issue' -- one conjunct of a compound condition, which a whole-condition mutation could not distinguish.
One MEMBER of the closed-state set, not the whole set. A merged merge request would report 'unknown' while 'closed' still worked, so the existing Closed case cannot see this.
The GitLab spelling of the open state, isolated from GitHub's. Same shape as M18 on the other set.

mutations.rationale: Precedence rule 1 for normalize_status: provider LABEL mappings are consulted before the raw status. Disabling the arm makes a labelled item fall to its raw status or to the state fallback.

Only PLAIN scalars get implicit resolution; a QUOTED "yes" is the string "yes" in both engines. Dropping the style gate re-resolves quoted scalars, so '"yes"' becomes the bool key "true". This is the clause that separates `- yes` from `- "yes"`, and no other mutation reaches it.

R3 tag DISPATCH: PyYAML 1.1 resolves yes/no/on/off as booleans; go-yaml 1.2 calls them strings. Restricting the pattern to the 1.2 spellings reverts exactly that, turning the key "false" back into "no". Targeted at dispatch rather than at True/False capitalisation, which normKey would flatten (see $limitation).
R3: `12:00:00` is the integer 43200 to PyYAML and a plain string to go-yaml. Dropping the sexagesimal branch indexes "12:00:00" instead of "43200".

The dotless-exponent resolver rule: PyYAML's float pattern REQUIRES a literal dot, which is why `1e3` is the STRING '1e3'. Making the dot optional floats it to 1000.0. This is the resolver, not the formatter -- R4 could not catch it.

The other half of the same rule, isolated: PyYAML's exponent requires an explicit SIGN, so `1.5e8` is a string while `1.5e+8` is a float. Making the sign optional floats 1.5e8. M24 keeps the sign requirement and M25 keeps the dot requirement, so neither subsumes the other.

mutations.rationale: PyYAML reads `010` as OCTAL 8. Falling through to the decimal branch indexes "10". The review's note that octal was 'already right' held only because go-yaml happens to agree here; nothing pinned it until now.

PyYAML 1.1 does NOT recognise the YAML-1.2 `0o10` spelling: it is the STRING '0o10'. go-yaml resolves it to 8. Accepting the 0o form here reintroduces go-yaml's reading of a scalar the real resolver leaves alone.
R4 numeric formatter, NaN half. Declared expected survivor -- see expected_survivor_reason.
mutations.expected_survivor_reason: MEASURED, not assumed. The input class is 'a float scalar that resolves to NaN' -- in this corpus the `.nan` entry of pyyaml_scalars.yaml. normKey lowercases AFTER pythonStr, so Python's 'nan' and Go's 'NaN' both fold to the index key 'nan' and no comparison can separate them. Removing the branch outright does not help either: FormatFloat yields 'NaN', the exponent Cut finds no 'e' and returns early, so the old 'NaN.0' shape cannot reappear through this path. NaN spelling is therefore genuinely unobservable at the index, and listing it as a kill would be a fake kill. The observable half of R4 is pinned by M29 (the '+' in '+Inf' survives folding) and M32 (the missing '.0').

mutations.rationale: R4: Python renders positive infinity as 'inf'; Go's %g renders '+Inf'. The leading '+' survives normKey's lowercasing, so this is a genuine key divergence rather than a capitalisation one.

R4: CPython switches to scientific notation at exponent >= 16. Moving the threshold to 17 renders 1.0e+16 as '10000000000000000.0' instead of '1e+16'. The fixture carries 1.0e+15 AND 1.0e+16 precisely so the boundary is observable from both sides.
The other end of the same switch, isolated from M30: 1.0e-4 must stay fixed ('0.0001') while 1.0e-5 goes scientific. Moving the low bound renders 0.0001 as '1e-04'.
Python renders an integral float as '1.0', not '1'. Dropping the suffix collapses the float 1.0 onto the same key as the integer 1 -- two different YAML scalars becoming one index entry.

R2: PyYAML assigns duplicate keys in turn, so the LAST value wins. Keeping the first makes the replaced [Alpha] survive -- 'alpha' reappears in the index, which is the silent-wrong-value shape the ruling said could not be merely declared.

The POSITION half of R2, which the value half cannot reach: a Python dict keeps a duplicated key at its FIRST appearance. Moving it to the end reorders todo after done, and because the fixture puts 'Charlie' under both, last-wins indexing then resolves charlie to todo instead of done.

mutations.rationale: R1 BLOCKER: `statuses: [a, b]` -- the classic indentation slip -- raises AttributeError in Python. Swallowing it builds four empty indexes and classifies every work item as issue/unknown while reporting success: silent metric corruption during coexistence.

The COUNTERPART to M35, and the reason `or {}` matters: an EMPTY list is falsy and must be swallowed silently, not rejected. Treating every container as truthy over-applies the R1 fix and turns a valid config into an error -- a failure mode the blocker fix could otherwise introduce unnoticed.

Python's `for raw in values` over a STRING yields its characters, so `todo: notalist` indexes n, o, t, a, l, i, s. Removing the branch turns that into a TypeError -- a loud failure where Python quietly indexes seven keys.

mutations.replace:
keys := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
		return keys, nil
mutations.rationale: Iterating a MAPPING yields its KEYS. Returning nothing silently drops every value under a category written as a mapping instead of a list.

`todo: 5` raises TypeError ('int' object is not iterable). Returning nothing instead reports a healthy load for a config Python rejects -- and the outcome field is what makes the difference visible, since both would otherwise show an empty index.

R5: Python's str.lower() is FULL case mapping. strings.ToLower folds 'İ' (U+0130) to a bare 'i' while Python produces 'i' + U+0307, so the label 'İSSUE' MATCHES in Go and MISSES in Python. Labels are user-controlled provider text; no malice required. The discarded caser keeps the import used: without it the mutated file fails to BUILD, which the harness reports as INVALID -- a mutation that never ran, not a kill.

The locale choice, pinned explicitly because it is a TRAP: cases.Lower(language.Turkish) is byte-identical to the broken strings.ToLower on 'İ', so picking Turkish -- which looks reasonable when the motivating character is Turkish -- silently reproduces the very defect M40 fixes. Python's str.lower() is locale-independent; Und is the locale-independent caser.
